reviews.text:
Disappointing. I was excited when I found a diet app that included a workout plan that takes minimal equipment. The choice of diet type (traditional, keto, clean eating, etc) is great too but that’s where the pros end. There’s no way to preview meals in advance so you can adjust when needed or pre-prep. I’m a teacher and a busy mom. I don’t have two hours in the morning to prep and cook meals for the day. The recipes are poorly written with typos that are hard to understand and very unclear portions. They seem to default to 1 serving size recipes with the ability to adjust up for more portions but a pound of pasta is NOT one portion, nor is 7 lbs of pork. The organization of the recipes is lousy and you cannot make and log your own recipes. When you try to swap a meal, you chose which meal you’re swapping and then get a random list of recipes that includes dressings, sauces, and weird sides that are NOT reasonable or healthy choices. It’s like they pulled in a bunch of random recipes from the internet. The workouts are ok if you know nothing about working out, but you can’t preview the workout to see what equipment you might need and you can’t swap out the workout or log something different. I swim a lot in the summer and ride bicycles. I also walk at least 10,000 steps a day. You can set a step goal and supposedly pull the step info from your phone, however the app does not update regularly so I still don’t know what it’s actually logging. Additionally, I don’t always carry my phone, I wear a Fitbit instead, but you can’t log additional steps in the app and since it doesn’t seem to pull the information from your phone like it’s supposed to, again, I have no idea what it’s really logging. Finally, when setting up your plan, you set your goals, choose your diet plan and approximate fitness level and you’re locked in. You can’t adjust ANYTHING if it’s not working for you (except to swap meals). The projected date to meet the goal is completely unrealistic. It told me I could lose 50 lbs in 40 days. That is NOT realistic in any world so I figured it was an error and it meant a year out, but can’t be certain. I’d bail on the whole app but I paid for a 1 year subscription, so I figure I’ll use it for the workouts but I’m having trouble sticking to that because I can’t accurately log anything, so how can I say it’s working or not working?

Update: I did a VERY little research and found the exact recipes that were downloaded from the internet for the meal plans. There’s no research-based anything going into the meal plans, but most likely an algorithm that pulls recipes from the bank of recipes based on calorie count. It wouldn’t be so bad if the recipes included ALL the information, but either someone keyed them in or they were downloaded using technology. Either way, no one bothered to proofread the recipes or instructions. 

I can’t help but think that this app was developed by someone with no real experience or knowledge about weight loss, and it’s all based on superficial research information and algorithms.
